steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
The standard for 10G-PON is ITU-T G.987.

The asymmetric version of 10G-PON is specified as XG-PON1. It has 10 Gbit/s downstream and 2.5 Gbit/s upstream. The nominal line rate is 9.95328 Gbit/s downstream and 2.48832 Gbit/s upstream.

A symmetric version of 10G-PON is also proposed, as XG-PON2, with 10 Gbit/s upstream. But this would need more expensive burst-mode lasers on the optical network terminals (ONTs) so they can deliver the upstream transmission speed. There is also another symmetric 10G-PON standard, XGS-PON, which is ITU-T G.9807.1 and was approved 2016-06-22.

- coexistence / comparison
  - framing "G-PON like", different wavelengths, WDM separates them; G-PON subscribers can upgrade incrementally, GPON users stay on original OLT
  - G-PON standard = G.984
  - compare IEEE 802.3av 10G-EPON (Ethernet), upstream 1 and 10 Gbit/s
  - 1577 nm down / 1270 nm up vs 1490 nm down / 1310 nm up -> coexist on same fibre

### G.987

- family defining XG-PON, four recommendations
  - G.987: definitions, abbreviations, acronyms, 2010
  - G.987.1: general requirements (2010-01-13); services, UNIs, SNIs, deployment configurations
  - G.987.2: PMD layer (2010-01-13, updated 2010-10-07); from G.984.2; asymmetric only
  - G.987.3: TC specifications (2010-10-07)

### G.988

- companion standard, ONU management and control interface, referred to by G.987
- G.988: OMCI specification (2010-10-07)

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
The standard for 10G-PON is ITU-T G.987.

The asymmetric version of 10G-PON is specified as XG-PON1. It has 10 Gbit/s downstream and 2.5 Gbit/s upstream. The nominal line rate is 9.95328 Gbit/s downstream and 2.48832 Gbit/s upstream.

A symmetric version of 10G-PON is also proposed, as XG-PON2, with 10 Gbit/s upstream. But this would need more expensive burst-mode lasers on the optical network terminals (ONTs) so they can deliver the upstream transmission speed. There is also another symmetric 10G-PON standard, XGS-PON, which is ITU-T G.9807.1 and was approved 2016-06-22.

The framing is "G-PON like", but it uses different wavelengths from G-PON, and a WDM is used to separate them. This is so that G-PON subscribers can be upgraded to 10G-PON incrementally, while the GPON users continue on the original optical line terminal (OLT). The standard for G-PON is G.984. This can be compared to the IEEE 802.3av standard for 10G-EPON, which is based on Ethernet and has standardised upstream rates of both 1 Gbit/s and 10 Gbit/s. The wavelengths of 10 gigabit PON are 1577 nm down and 1270 nm up, which is different from GPON and EPON, which use 1490 nm down and 1310 nm up, and this allows it to coexist on the same fibre with either of the gigabit PONs.

### G.987

G.987 is an ITU-T Recommendation family that defines this access network standard, which is referred to as XG-PON. There are four recommendations in it:

G.987: 10-Gigabit-capable passive optical network (XG-PON) systems: Definitions, Abbreviations, and Acronyms, 2010.

G.987.1: General requirements of 10G-PON systems, approved 2010-01-13. It includes examples of services, user network interfaces (UNIs) and service node interfaces (SNIs), and also the main deployment configurations that network operators requested.

G.987.2: Physical media dependent (PMD) layer specification, approved 2010-01-13 and updated 2010-10-07. It describes a flexible optical fibre access network that is an evolutionary development from G.984.2. In the current version it is asymmetric only.

G.987.3: Transmission convergence (TC) specifications, approved 2010-10-07.

### G.988

There is a companion ITU-T standard too, which defines a management and control interface for administering optical network units, and the G.987 recommendations refer to it.

G.988: ONU management and control interface (OMCI) specification, approved 2010-10-07.
